title: How do we write a crore and an arab as powers of ten?
description: A lakh is a hundred times a thousand, which is ten to the power two times ten to the power three. Each next Indian name is a hundred times the one before, so we find the powers for a crore, an arab, a kharab and a neel. Keeko doubts how the powers combine.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying powers of ten adds the powers, because the tens are counted. Watch for students who multiply the powers, for example two times five, instead of adding them.

source: Starting from a lakh as 10² × 10³, find the powers of 10 for a crore, an arab, a kharab and a neel
video_script.why: Each Indian name is a hundred times the one before, and multiplying powers of ten adds the powers, so each name raises the power by two.
video_script.substitution: Write each name as a hundred times the name before it, then add two to the power of the name before it.
video_script.anchor: the Indian names lakh, crore, arab, kharab and neel
video_script.wrong_answer: a crore is ten to the power ten
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the powers, two times five, and says a crore is 10 to the power 10. But 10 to the power 10 is a thousand crore; multiplying powers of ten adds the powers, so a crore is 10 to the power 7.
video_script.payoff_line: A hundred times the one before adds two to the power

final_answer.value: Crore 10 to the power 7, arab 10 to the power 9, kharab 10 to the power 11, neel 10 to the power 13
final_answer.spoken: A crore is ten to the power seven. An arab is ten to the power nine. A kharab is ten to the power eleven. A neel is ten to the power thirteen.

maths_rules: the slip: 2 × 5 = 10 gives 10¹⁰, which is 1000 crore
video_script.design: A row of tens is drawn for each name, and every new name adds two tens to the row before it. The working area writes the sum of the powers in a second colour.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a crore is ten to the power ten, because two times five is ten.
<bookmark mark='big'/>But ten to the power ten is a thousand crore, which is far too big.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Multiplying powers of ten counts the tens, so we add the powers, never multiply them.
